title: Cold Open: The Muffin He Left
palette: Pre-dawn blue-gray woods, cold ash and dew silver, one warm amber pool on the folded bandages and Tupperware muffin
music: how-i-wish - near-instrumental, distant and hollow, melody carried under the empty space where John slept
summary: Dawn at Wiley's woods camp. Obi wakes wrecked from Bitter Dividend. John is gone — but half his bandages are left folded for Obi's strap-wounds, beside a Tupperware with a single muffin. Wiley: 'he left you breakfast, man.' Care even in leaving. Title card.

title: The Receipt and the Wristband
palette: Flat morning overcast, greasy paper-bag tan, receipt-thermal white, muted denim and camp canvas
music: how-i-wish - sparse acoustic fragments, stopping dead whenever the timestamp is read aloud
summary: Seth arrives with the P. Terry's receipt and hospital wristband, both stamped twenty minutes in the future, Integrity 100%. Obi insists on leading a search he can't lead and refuses help. Seth's flat skepticism ('they're not that interesting, dude') vs. the stamp that bothers him. The Twenty-Minute Log begins on the greasy bag. Mark films everything — camera arc step 1.

title: The Rumor Telegraph
palette: Corridor daylight, sun-bleached asphalt gray, storefront signage color pops, heat-haze white
music: starts - full-band ignition hit on the act break, then cat4 - sly walking-bass suspicion under the montage
summary: Montage west-to-east down the corridor. The contradiction machine: John's hospitalized / got a maintenance job / went to Round Rock, which everyone agrees is worse than missing. Log entries accumulate on the degrading bag. The search has become official.

title: Norm's Camp at the Sterzing Box
palette: Electrical-box industrial green, tarp blue, extension-cord orange, late-morning contrast shadows
music: cat4 - stripped to percussion and muted stabs, sketchy-approach treatment
summary: The crew works Norm's electrical-box camp. Infection-source thread touched, not resolved; one Sadi-finger beat silences Truth exactly once. The reframing clue: John was here asking Norm how HE got treated. He isn't fleeing — he's questing alone. Log entry: 'Norm sneezed. Circle it.'

title: Hospital Stonewall
palette: Fluorescent institutional white-green, laminate beige, privacy-glass frost, one red EXIT sign
music: hey-joe - protest-blues shuffle against the privacy desk, with a diegetic cieeffoeeyy fragment as the A.T.T. improved-hold-music
summary: Full bureaucracy kit: 'Are you family?' / 'I'm his... documentarian.' / '...Sir.' The A.T.T. phone-tree ('WE IMPROVE WHAT YOU MEANT') improves the crew's messages back at them; the pharmacist can neither confirm nor deny that a Walgreens exists. Mark leaves the camera in the truck — this scene exists in-world but not in his footage. Midpoint turn: John checked in, heard 'we don't know if you're contagious,' and walked out AMA. His motive lands.

title: Beat: Help Without Forgiveness
palette: Parking-lot dusk gray, sodium-lamp amber edge, two figures in negative space
music: how-i-wish - single guitar figure, then silence for the ask itself
summary: The short beat: Obi, neck feathers down, asks Hunter to check his reasoning. Help granted, forgiveness explicitly withheld. The apology stays incomplete and the scene is better for it.

title: The Twenty-Minute Stakeout
palette: Golden-hour picnic-table orange fading to teal dusk, translucent grease-bag glow held up to the light
music: cat4 - tense held-breath reduction, dropping out entirely for the Bellweather kettle beat
summary: Five people stare at an empty picnic table while Seth narrates 'any second now.' The theory half-works (fresh traces, missed him by minutes) and half-fails, exactly once each — Bellweather ambiguity locked. On the walk out, the single Bellweather cameo: descaling a kettle on the creek bank. 'The kettle doesn't know either.' She never offers tea.

title: The Footage Scrub
palette: Laptop-screen blue on a dark truck cab, timeline-scrubber red, monitor glow on Mark's glasses
music: fog - slow existential build with one quoted instrumental puddle phrase inside it, Ep1 callback
summary: Night. Mark scrubs his own exploitation reel, watching himself set the camera down too late, over and over — camera arc step 2, half-filming himself watching. A bell rings, faint, source-less; he sets the camera down before the moment for the first time in his life. Twenty minutes later he finds the tell: 'soaked in bleach, baby' — the bleach foot-soak riff means an upstream spring.

title: Upstream: Into New Territory
palette: Limestone white and live-oak green, graffiti-wall color burst at Gus Fruh, bone-dry creek-bed chalk, no skyline
music: starts - reprise as patient trail-walking pulse, dry-mineral percussion treatment
summary: The named route by land with Wiley — Gus Fruh's graffiti wall, false-find at Twin Falls, Sculpture Falls — while TK poles the raft up the waterless creek bed ('River gets a vote.' 'There's no river, man.' 'Unanimous, then.'). Wiley's gospel wobble: 'I go to the woods to hear myself, man. He went to stop.' Documentary lenses on limestone; the creek's just introverted.

title: The Seep Pool
palette: Bleach-white spring water, cool shade under the Hill of Life, John's skin tones pale against wet limestone
music: how-i-wish - full statement at last, the search motif resolving onto the found man
summary: John at the seep pool below the Hill of Life, feet in spring water, gallows engine at full throttle — 'morphine and monkey pox,' tangent-stacking into Drew Carey mid-tears. The rumor line lands: 'you guys care enough about me to make up a fucking rumor?' His contagion confession — exile-as-protection — out loud at last.

title: The Climax of Touch
palette: Warming afternoon gold breaking into the shade, bandage white, dry-muffin brown as the warmest color on screen
music: my-muffin-is-dry - full vocal cue under the hand-take, 'I'm scared, I'm stoned, I'm still in the fight'
summary: Obi crosses the distance and takes John's bandaged hand knowing what it might cost. MRSA truth dramatized — treatable, doxycycline works, precautions suffice, not poison — via John reciting his allergy list to the on-call resident in full Drew Carey cadence, laughing and crying in one take. Mark hands John's own line back: 'maybe you need to care about yourself more.' The Tupperware surfaces from Obi's pack — the muffin, carried the whole search, genuinely dry. Camera stays in the truck.

title: The Carry Home / Coda
palette: Warm rain silver-gold on the trail for thirty seconds only, then evening hospital-room lamplight, IV-bag translucence
music: lance-aleks-dancing-in-the-rain - thirty seconds only, cut clean before euphoria overclaims; then room tone and a single faint bell
summary: The group carries John as John carried Obi; Obi lets Hunter steady him. Obi's near-credit: 'The sky drew it. Mark held the pen adjacent.' One paid-for shaft of warm rain. Coda: hospital room, evening — John's IV bag drips in perfect 4/4. Mark notices. Mark does not film it. A bell rings somewhere, faint. The weather is one degree kinder. No answers about Bellweather.

title: Credits + Post-Credit Tag: The Monkey Tree
palette: Credits on black, then dusk green-black off Azie Morton, one small brass bell catching the last light
music: gator2 - fragment as a low sting under the bell, silence before and after
summary: Credits roll. Post-credit tag: behind Barton Springs Pool's south side, first-ever glimpse of the Monkey Tree — a single small bell hung in its branches. No wind. It rings once. Documentary fact card: hydrologists trace Barton Springs' water with dye — rain that falls miles away surfaces here days later. Springs don't predict rain; they live downstream of it.
